research_updates.title: Permit and construction audit found one valued company-county permit
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: BCDCOG Construction Quarterly archive and annual reports, Berkeley County permitting/planning pages, county council packets, and exact web searches for Google Facilities, Maguro, Arum, 1669 Garrott, Mount Holly Commerce Park, and data center across 2007-2026. The only addressable Google permit value found was the December 4, 2020 $20,749,187 entry. No permit number, address, contractor, final cost, phase, hours, worker count, payroll, invoice, supplier residence, or selected-building crosswalk was public. Construction job-years therefore use a separately governed low-confidence benchmark rather than being called observed employment.

research_updates.title: Assessor audit isolated one Google-linked expansion-land account
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Berkeley County property-card search, indexed property cards, tax histories, deed/plat references, owner/address/TMS searches, and linked county GIS context. Queries included Google, Maguro Enterprises, Arum Composites, 1600 Amphitheatre, 1669/1684 Garrott, 251 Lillie, 516 Parker Simms, and TMS 211-00-02-078, -092, and -219. The live search endpoint returned a Cloudflare JavaScript challenge to noninteractive review, while indexed card 211-00-02-092 supplied exact 2024-2025 land values and paid taxes. Its acquisition note identifies five parcels bought for $25.8 million in total, but mixed deed lines prevent parcel-level allocation. Parent operating-campus, personal-property, FILOT, and full Arum/Maguro account rolls remain unresolved; former Maguro water-tank parcel -219 is now county-owned and excluded.

research_updates.title: Incentive agreement audit found legal mechanisms but no realized cost ledger
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Berkeley County Council agendas, minutes, ordinance text links, ACFRs, economic-development fund notes, Commerce Coordinating Council reports, Enterprise Zone reports, and exact searches for Maguro, Project Eagle, Project Linden, Google, fee in lieu, FILOT, special source revenue credit, multi-county park, and recapture across 2006-2025. Bills 18-45 and 20-53 confirm FILOT/credit mechanisms and amendments, but no public same-year credit used, tax avoided, cash payment, recipient receipt, clawback, or marginal service cost was found. Secondary estimates were not substituted for the missing executed schedules. The public-cost model is only an equal-cost threshold tied to one paid parcel account, not an incentive value or fiscal surplus.

research_updates.title: Water and environmental audit separates actual groundwater use from legal capacity
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: SC DES Trident groundwater evaluations, Santee basin plan, permit/public-notice portal, board minutes, wastewater and drinking-water searches, Google environmental reporting, and exact identifiers Maguro, 08IN015, 08IN015G01, 1669 Garrott, 19-RFR-48, withdrawal, discharge, stormwater, and wastewater across 2007-2025. Direct results are 2.74 million gallons of 2021 reported groundwater withdrawal and a 549 million-gallon annual permit ceiling. The DES public-notice search requires interactive state and supplied no export in this review; board minutes confirm the permit challenge was withdrawn but add no use value. Operator water-consumption values are wider reporting totals and are kept modeled/unallocated. No discharge, sewer bill, potable/reclaimed split, peak demand, meter, cooling-cycle, or selected-building allocation was public.

research_updates.title: Commissioned economic-impact outputs remain source-modeled and channel-separated
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: the full six-page Google/Deloitte South Carolina impact study, source notes, IMPLAN methodology disclosure, Google state pages, Census/BEA/BLS public series, and searches for jobs, direct employees, contractors, payroll, labor income, GDP, supplier purchases, local contractors, and household spending. The study reports 2021-2023 annual averages of approximately $626 million GDP, 6,430 jobs, and $411 million labor income, with direct/indirect/induced channels. These are reproduced only in modeled synthesis with the report's state/data-center boundary and rounding; they are not observed campus payroll, headcount, procurement, tax revenue, selected-building effects, or causal impacts. No company supplier ledger, vendor residence, local-capture share, actual payroll, benefits, or annual-average establishment FTE was public.

research_updates.title: Electricity, fuel, emissions, and cooling audit found no facility consumption ledger
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: BCWS landfill-gas page, Berkeley Electric and Santee Cooper tariffs/planning documents, Google efficiency and energy pages, SC DES air-permit/public-notice searches, EPA facility/name/address searches, and exact queries for Maguro, Google, 1669 Garrott, load, kWh, MW, PUE, generators, diesel, NOx, CO2e, and emissions across 2007-2026. The county confirms a four-year landfill-gas-credit relationship but no Google quantity or payment. The impact study reports PUE and carbon-free-energy matching at a wider data-center boundary, retained only in the exact proposal ledger. No meter, tariff assignment, bill, peak load, annual electricity, generator inventory, fuel burn, actual emissions, market-based emissions, avoided-emissions counterfactual, heat rejection, or selected-building cooling load was found; none is inferred from renewable nameplate capacity.

research_updates.title: Infrastructure and public-cost audit rejects park-wide allocation
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Berkeley County ACFRs, capital-project and debt notes, BCWS capital documents, county contract register, Mount Holly Commerce Park improvement contracts, county council records, and bond/loan searches. The ACFR describes a $500,000 annual park-revenue transfer until an approximately $4.8 million water/sewer amount and a Mount Holly pump-station loan; the contract register lists a $5,447,237 park-improvement contract. These values serve multiple park users and lack a Google beneficiary, cost-causation, service-area, reimbursement, or building allocation, so they are not project records or public-cost estimates.

research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Berkeley County School District, Berkeley Electric Cooperative, Home Telecom, local nonprofits, Google community pages, and the Deloitte impact study for grants, recipients, dates, purposes, and overlap. The 2013 greater-than-$885,000, 2019-forward approximately $500,000, and 2022-2023 approximately $2.8 million figures overlap across periods or recipients and are tagged nonadditive. research_updates.title: Metric-by-metric disposition preserves native boundaries
research_updates.notes: Investment: retained as campus cumulative observations and separate commitments. Construction: one county-reported permit retained; workers, payroll, duration, final cost, and local supplier spend remain gaps. Suppliers/household spending: only commissioned IMPLAN indirect/induced channels are modeled; no purchase ledger or residence capture is claimed. Operations: greater-than-200 people is a 2018 campus snapshot; state contribution outputs remain modeled, not headcount/payroll. Fiscal: one Arum land parcel has exact 2024-2025 values and paid taxes; campus FILOT/personal-property/receipt totals remain missing. Public costs: agreements and park infrastructure are contextual; only a same-scope equal-cost threshold is modeled. Resources: groundwater actual and permit capacity are direct; water consumption is modeled at source scope; electricity, wastewater, emissions, generators, and cooling remain gaps. Community: direct and cumulative funding is retained with overlap warnings. County GDP/employment/wage: descriptive matched comparisons are modeled with robustness checks, no causal attribution, and are not a Google effect.

research_updates.title: Adversarial corrective review completed
research_updates.notes: A genuinely new second-pass review reopened the 2013, 2018, and 2021 Commerce pages; all six impact-study pages and footnotes; SC DES name/address/permit searches; Berkeley County FILOT/Project Eagle/Project Linden searches; BCDCOG permit archive searches; and Arum/Maguro assessor-card searches. Two candidate actuals were removed: the 2018 page says total investment would reach approximately $2.4 billion only after its announced expansion, and the 2021 page says the expansion brings state investment to $2.9 billion; neither supports a realized pre-announcement $2.4 billion record. The three commissioned contribution estimates were renamed from operating metrics because the report explicitly includes construction, engineering, networking, renewable-energy, security, and service activity, and jobs remain jobs rather than FTE. The environmental proposal now uses the report footnote's state/all-data-center scope and includes exact prospective scope, catalog, claim, and regression payloads. Final reconciled account: 23 fragment records and one baseline record yield 24 merged records, 20 reported actuals, four source projections, and 12 modeled syntheses after six environmental values became direct records and two deterministic water carry-through rows were retired. All eight account categories and all three descriptive county modules are populated, but direct evidence remains incomplete in every category. Unresolved gaps remain the operating-campus and personal-property account universe, realized FILOT and credit schedules, full recipient receipts, observed construction/workforce/payroll/supplier ledgers, electricity and utility bills, wastewater, generators and emissions, cooling loads, actual marginal public costs, annual community reconciliation, and causal county effects. Status: adversarial_review_complete_reconciled; accepted under Contract 3.1.0.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. interval.interpretation: Range across K=3, K=10, South Carolina K=5, and five leave-one-out donor specifications; not statistical confidence.

modeled_syntheses.confidence_rationale: Pre-2007 real-GDP growth paths fit, but industrial growth, continuous expansions, and spillovers prevent causal attribution.
modeled_syntheses.decision_relevance: Describes Berkeley County real-GDP divergence without assigning it to Google.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Causal treatment isolation, sector controls, expansion timing, spillover rules, placebo inference, and alternative donor designs

assumptions: Matching uses 2001-2006 normalized log paths and a 2006 base.
Study counties are excluded and donor population ratio is 0.35-2.5.
The 2007 anchor is not assumed to isolate treatment.

limitations: Descriptive, not a Google effect.
Concurrent industrial growth and expansions confound attribution.
Sensitivity envelope is not statistical confidence.

modeled_scope_note: Foundational accounts re-audited under study-modeling-policy 1.3.0 after renewed direct-evidence searches. Apple Mesa retains three narrowly scoped business-personal-property FTZ counterfactuals from its project fragment; Switch Citadel retains four exact fiscal arithmetic or break-even syntheses; Digital Crossroad Hammond retains two two-account paid-tax arithmetic or break-even syntheses from its project fragment. All other legacy foundational estimates were removed because direct inputs, project scope, time profiles, local allocation, causal identification, or decision relevance were not defensible. Reported observations, forecasts, and remaining models stay separate. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00116005354: Post-audit last-resort modeling gate for Apple Maiden. No estimate survives: campus and company/county evidence cannot be allocated to IM3 building 00116005354, annual incentive observations have unresolved municipal and service-cost gaps, contractor identities lack spend and geography, employment snapshots lack payroll and residence, and county aggregates lack a defensible treatment share or counterfactual. The direct-evidence fragment records every candidate-specific rejection and leaves unresolved metrics as gaps rather than fabricating building shares, tax receipts, utility use, multipliers or causal effects. prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Last-resort NAP7 modeling pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact, same-property-account fiscal-year 2027 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed property-tax bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, resource, community and county outcome candidates were rejected because compatible NAP7 inputs or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00214321737: Last-resort Markley Lowell model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact same-account FY2026 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed four-quarter real-property bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, fiscal-net, resource, community and each GDP, employment and wage candidate are rejected separately in the evidence fragment because compatible inputs, scope alignment, non-overlap proof or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00300974499: Corrective policy-1.3.0 synthesis. Three legacy combined real-and-personal-property FTZ counterfactuals are superseded by narrower business-personal-property-only estimates because the Apple BPP account directly exhibits the 5% assessment ratio while the real-property account has a different valuation base. The replacements hold observed effective tax rates and full cash value constant and isolate only the assessment-ratio component; they are not cash grants, audited forgone-revenue amounts or net fiscal benefits. All other legacy Apple Mesa estimates fail the direct-evidence, scope, time-profile, geography or decision-relevance gates and are marked for removal in the evidence fragment. prj_study_im3_building_00359930465: Post-fifth-pass last-resort modeling gate for Equinix Seattle SE3 retains eight bounded syntheses. Construction is represented separately by the AGC/DJC $50 million-$100 million award-category sensitivity and a 50,482-hours wage benchmark; neither is audited spend or certified payroll. Opening evidence for 24-hour operations and security supports only a conditional one-active-post coverage floor and wage-cost benchmark, not observed posts, headcount, payroll or total staffing. The 2011 lease's up-to-9-MW allocation remains a 25/50/100-percent throughput sensitivity, with separate statewide/tariff price and eGRID NWPP location-based emissions benchmarks that are not bills, measured emissions or market-based results. A medium-confidence identity sets the 2026 same-account assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even threshold equal to the exact landlord-parcel bill; it does not estimate actual public cost, tenant pass-through, cash receipt, recipient distribution or net fiscal impact. A supplier/non-labor residual is rejected because the award category does not define cost coverage and the reported hours do not establish complete labor coverage; community and causal county-effect candidates still fail for lack of compatible inputs or identification. prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00388148510: Project-scoped modeled synthesis for TierPoint Little Rock. Eleven resolved-year real-property taxable values are multiplied by signed code 03/33 school, city, and county millage components; 2025 is excluded because its observed Amount Due does not disclose the underlying revised taxable value. A conditional zero-leave FTE-equivalent floor translates the facility-specific 2012 onsite NOC staffed 24/7/365 statement without claiming employee headcount or payroll. Two low-confidence engineering sensitivities use one, not both, of the redundant 3,000 kVA utility transformers and expose hypothetical power-factor, utilization, and PUE assumptions. Every estimate is modeled_not_observed_or_audited and excluded from sourced-record counts, cash receipts, realized-benefit totals, and net-fiscal claims. prj_study_im3_building_00397914434: Corrective last-resort modeling pass for Apple Prineville. Five narrow, unallocated syntheses now survive: a same-land-account tax-payment break-even identity; a 2018 campus/company payroll sensitivity anchored to the reported 100 jobs and three official BLS Central Oregon occupation benchmarks; FY2025 campus electricity-cost sensitivity using EIA Oregon customer-class averages after PacifiCorp direct-access tariffs proved noncomputable from public inputs; deterministic FY2025 average-load conversion; and an EPA eGRID location-based electricity-emissions factor sensitivity. None is allocated to IM3 building 00397914434. The cost range is not Apple's bill, the payroll range is not observed payroll, and the emissions range is not Apple's market-based Scope 2 result and preserves Apple's 100 percent renewable-electricity claim. Investment, construction, supplier, community, net-fiscal and causal county-outcome candidates remain rejected for missing scope-compatible inputs or identification. prj_study_im3_building_00438078069: Second corrective modeled-synthesis pass for Meta Altoona. Exact annual active-account property-tax aggregations and the 2024 equal-cost public-service threshold implement study-modeling-policy 1.3.0; deterministic average-load conversions, labor-hour equivalence, explicitly stylized payroll sensitivities, and noncausal county comparison gaps retain every input and overlap limitation. All results remain unallocated to the selected 315,400-square-foot IM3 building. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00472761713: Third-pass modeled synthesis for NYSE Group's U.S. Liquidity Center in Mahwah. Three 2025 parcel-levy allocations use certified recipient rates that reconcile exactly to the direct parcel bill; a same-account break-even identity states the public-cost decision threshold without estimating cost or net benefit. A wide 28 MW utilization sensitivity exposes the theoretical annual site-electricity scale, a four-quarter WIPP conversion preserves parcel and period limits, and a zero-leave 24x7 support-coverage equivalent remains location-unallocated. All estimates are modeled_not_observed_or_audited and excluded from direct-record totals. prj_study_im3_building_00499403180: Third corrective synthesis for Microsoft's Central Washington portfolio and unallocated MWH campus context. Source-modeled EY/IMPLAN operating and construction contribution outputs are preserved at Chelan-Douglas-Grant scope without conversion to selected-building effects. The direct-compensation proxy uses the reported 377 jobs and rounded $93,000 compensation at the same regional scope. Campus electricity savings are converted only to an average-load equivalent; QWRU water availability is converted only from cubic meters to gallons. Four complete MWH real-plus-personal tax-year totals and four equal-cost identities are retained for 2022-2025, but no actual public cost or net fiscal sign is asserted. Six county comparison gaps are low-confidence descriptive benchmarks for the separate 2007 Columbia event and 2015 MWH context, never causal effects. All estimates are unallocated to the 143,439-square-foot IM3 footprint and subject to explicit non-additivity. prj_study_im3_building_00500820007: Third corrective modeled-synthesis gate under project-worker research Contract 3.1.0 and study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Seventeen bounded syntheses survive: nine exact Winner-only annual paid-property-tax aggregations for 2017-2025, the 2025 same-scope marginal-service-cost break-even identity, one deterministic 2018 gross-before-realized-abatement counterfactual, one low-confidence 2020 operating-payroll sensitivity, three 2024 resource syntheses, and two explicitly noncausal 2024 county employment and wage comparison gaps anchored to the 2017 operating date. The electricity-cost central benchmark now uses the 2024 Texas industrial price; the 2024 commercial price is only a separate class sensitivity. The location-based emissions estimate uses ERCT alone; Texas state-output geography is excluded from the interval. The county GDP comparison is rejected because its national +11.080969% gap reverses to -3.263943% with Texas-only donors, making a single central descriptive value misleading. MMI Southwest is excluded from every Winner aggregation. None is a new source observation, selected-building allocation, audited recipient receipt, actual payroll, utility bill, peak demand, actual or market-based emissions, observed public cost, net fiscal result or facility effect. Construction, supplier, induced, county-GDP, actual-bill, market-based-emissions and net-fiscal models remain rejected. prj_study_im3_building_00598261190: Dedicated last-resort model-eligibility pass for State Farm Olathe under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Four bounded syntheses are retained: the exact 2025 parcel-tax-payment identity as a same-account public-service-cost break-even threshold, plus low-confidence descriptive 2024 Johnson County GDP, employment and wage comparison gaps using the repository's pre-2016 inverse-distance benchmark. No estimate is an observed cost, net fiscal result or causal facility effect. Supplier/local-spend and community-allocation candidates, an HPIP credit counterfactual, and causal county designs are rejected because the project-specific inputs, scope matches, non-overlap proof or identification conditions recorded in the evidence fragment are absent. prj_study_im3_building_00610827836: Contract 3.1.0 modeled synthesis for Google Berkeley County. Estimates remain visibly modeled, retain native source boundaries, protect direct/indirect/induced aggregation, and do not allocate campus, state, parcel, or county values to the selected building. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00838817907: Corrective metric-specific synthesis for TierPoint Charlotte Center Park (CL4). Two independent staffing-equivalent sensitivities translate facility-specific continuous NOC and security coverage statements into the FTE capacity needed to cover one simultaneous post; neither is an observed employee count, the functions are not summed, and employer, overlap, shift, absence, residence and payroll remain unknown. A separate opening-configuration electricity sensitivity annualizes the directly reported 1.215 MW usable UPS capacity across utilization and PUE scenarios while checking the source-reported 3,000 kVA service capacity under power-factor assumptions. It is a theoretical nameplate envelope, not metered use, a true-value bound or an economic contribution. No model is created from 530 tons of cooling because electrical demand would require unobserved COP, part-load, redundancy and operating-hour inputs, and no model is created from generator counts, unit ratings, runtime or fuel storage because emergency standby nameplates do not measure annual operation. prj_study_im3_building_00844371952: Thirty residual modeled syntheses remain after the Google Bridgeport evidence audit. They retain published Deloitte/Google IMPLAN channels as source-modeled outputs, the lower-bound payroll annualization, exact annual paid-tax aggregations plus a 2025 equal-cost threshold, and three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps. Source-reported environmental values now live in the governed direct-evidence catalog. The models do not allocate campus/state results to the selected building, invent supplier spend/payroll/public costs, convert workers to job-years, estimate incentives or net fiscal impact, or treat source projections as actuals. prj_study_im3_building_00844389014: Second-pass model review retains one bounded resource identity only. It reproduces Google-reported 2024 Montgomery County water consumption as withdrawal minus discharge after converting displayed million-gallon values to gallons, with a rounding envelope. Direct searches of Clarksville utility/public-works pages, county stormwater records, TDEC/EPA portals and CDE/TVA materials did not surface a building meter, utility bill or a compatible canonical observed-water metric. The amount remains unallocated across the location and inventory buildings; discharge may be engineering-estimated. No transferred multiplier, supplier-retention assumption, energy proxy, fiscal result, public-cost threshold, payroll estimate or causal county outcome is modeled. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Residual synthesis after the SV1 public-source audit. It retains one exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold and three reproducible but low-confidence county comparison gaps. The county gaps use 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and an inverse-distance-weighted 20-county benchmark; very wide fit envelopes are retained because Santa Clara County matches poorly. No model converts capacity to consumption, permit value to jobs, or unidentified vendor and community activity to local benefits. prj_study_im3_building_00903236619: Third-pass modeled contribution review retains two low-confidence, last-resort sensitivities after direct-source exhaustion. The first converts the contractor-reported 1.4 MW whole-facility redundant available-power nameplate into annual electricity throughput at 25%, 50% and 100% utilization, with the high endpoint explicitly treated as a mathematical ceiling. It does not apply PUE because the source does not distinguish utility-input, critical IT or redundant-path capacity. The second combines the trade-reported approximately 70 electricians, the 234-day groundbreaking-to-report interval and BLS's near-period Detroit-area mean electrician wage into a 25%, 50% and 100% worker-duration wage-payroll sensitivity. It is limited to the reported electrician subset and excludes benefits, overtime, other trades and residence effects. No operating staffing, investment, supplier, community, fiscal/public-cost, emissions, water or county-effect model passes: no source requires continuous on-site coverage; the MCE $4.8 million field is undefined and postdates a site redesign; separate real and personal accounts lack bills and payments; the recovered City subsidy report omits this project; and no site-linked operating, recipient or counterfactual inputs exist. prj_study_im3_building_00978934687: Corrective residual synthesis for Digital Crossroad DX-1 under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Of 43 legacy estimates, none is retained unchanged: 41 are directed for removal and two are revised using the complete 2024-pay-2025 paid-tax base for the leasehold real account and DX Hammond JV LLC personal-property account. The revised contribution is an exact account-level aggregation across local taxing authorities, and the companion public-service-cost estimate is only the equal-cost break-even identity; neither is an audited recipient receipt, observed public cost or net fiscal result. New estimate IDs prevent silent mutation of the legacy base and their notes identify the superseded estimates for orchestrator reconciliation. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution. prj_study_im3_building_01132541700: Four bounded syntheses are retained after direct-record search: one deterministic conversion of Meta's rounded 2024 Henrico water-withdrawal observation and three governed, descriptive county comparison gaps. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. Every retained estimate is visibly modeled, unallocated to the selected building, non-additive, and noncausal. prj_study_im3_campus_00009474864: Fifteen unallocated modeled syntheses retained only after direct-evidence exhaustion: twelve exact same-year assessed-value aggregations, one source-projection payroll counterfactual, and two noncausal matched-county comparisons. Source-reported water, efficiency, carbon-free-energy, design and emissions values are direct governed records, not models. Supplier, electricity-use, tax-receipt, net-fiscal, public-cost, construction-payroll, social-return, and county-GDP candidates fail the project-anchor, scope, or sensitivity gates and remain documented gaps. prj_study_im3_campus_00019988712: Residual synthesis after the Meta Prineville direct-evidence audit. One medium-confidence unit conversion carries Meta's rounded 2024 facility-level water-withdrawal observation from megaliters to gallons because the shared direct register has no compatible annual-withdrawal metric. The three low-confidence county benchmark comparisons were removed: even with fit-sensitivity envelopes and explicit non-causal labels, they do not materially improve decisions about this campus and remain vulnerable to concurrent Meta expansions, Apple's separate campus and unrelated county changes. No supplier, construction, payroll, household-spending, tax-abatement, public-service-cost or fiscal-net model is retained because local inputs and same-scope evidence are insufficient. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Residual synthesis after the Google The Dalles public-source audit. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps are retained because the direct record does not identify causal county outcomes. Each benchmark uses the available 2001-2005 pre-opening history, excludes all study counties from a 20-county inverse-distance-weighted donor pool, and carries a fit-sensitivity envelope. No model converts broad investment or permit values to jobs, onsite contractor counts to supplier output, utility-system loads to campus consumption, tax bills to payments, or unmatched incentive formulas and public costs to a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_campus_00578435601: Directed fourth-pass model review retains eight bounded estimates grounded in published Douglas County or official national inputs: three presentation-preserving water-consumption conversions, one ECHO DMR-flow annualization, two county-M&O-only gross-levy counterfactuals on exempt personal property, one historical employee-threshold wage-bill sensitivity, and one permit-remodel construction-payroll sensitivity. Every estimate remains unallocated, non-audited, and outside direct-record totals. Tax counterfactuals are not bills, payments, tax avoided, realized abatement, net fiscal benefit, or all-jurisdiction liability; wage and construction results are transferred benchmarks rather than observed Google payroll; DMR flow is not consumption or utility-billed volume. Supplier retention, electricity use/cost, actual public-service cost, and causal county outcomes remain unsupported. prj_study_im3_campus_00675108684: Dedicated last-resort Boydton model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Retained syntheses are limited to exact arithmetic over cited compatible observations: a five-fiscal-year average of the operator-reported portfolio property-tax total, its explicitly conditional same-scope public-cost break-even identity, and annual sums of identified LVL/Herbert Fund 301 components. All remain unallocated, modeled rather than observed, and non-additive to their source totals. COF phase investment, operating headcount, construction, resources, suppliers, induced effects, causal comparisons and net fiscal impact were rejected because overlap, timing, scope or required project inputs remain unresolved.
legacy_first_entry_note: Google dates its exact mapped Berkeley County campus to 2007 and describes continuing operations. The county's nine current facilities do not establish a complete historical inventory or exclude earlier telecom, government, utility, university, healthcare, financial, or enterprise data centers.
scope_note: Provisional private-sector research candidate. Owner/operator history, project boundaries and lifecycle require review. Membership does not verify current operation or establish economic impact.
project_description: Google operates a multi-building data-center campus in Mount Holly Commerce Park near Moncks Corner, Berkeley County, South Carolina. The mapped inventory target is one building within that campus, so campus, company-state, later-expansion, parcel, and supporting-infrastructure values remain unallocated; the state reports the original $600 million site was established in 2007 and a second building announced in 2010 was operating by 2013. Later documented expansion announcements span 2013, 2018, 2021, 2024, and 2025.
